claims.claim: Astro7 renders HTML and supports server routes.
claims.finding: Official June22,2026 release describes prerendered HTML and server-routing features. It does not establish this site’s source cleanliness.

claims.claim: The Astro Node adapter supports standalone mode.
claims.finding: Official adapter docs explain a standalone server serving page, API, and asset routes. Local configuration selects this mode.

claims.claim: React provides interactive components within existing HTML.
claims.finding: Official documentation covers component-based interfaces, state updates, and adding React to an existing page. The local lockfile determines the installed version.

claims.claim: TypeScript7 has a native checker and TypeScript6 compatibility setup.
claims.finding: Microsoft shows @typescript/native aliased to TypeScript7 and typescript aliased to @typescript/typescript6, exposing tsc/tsc6. This matches the package files. Type correctness does not prove arithmetic.
Official documentation describes page interactions and browser testing. The article claims selected coverage rather than universal usability.

claims.claim: Automated accessibility checks do not replace manual assessment or inclusive user testing.
claims.finding: Official guidance recommends these complementary checks and states automated tests detect only some issues.
Official project describes a Vite-native test runner with backend support. Local tests and lockfile establish this project’s usage/version.
Official repository demonstrates image recognition using a browser worker. The current site’s paths and trigger are checked in local code.

claims.claim: Resolution, contrast, skew, and borders affect OCR.
claims.finding: Official guidance covers scaling, binarization, deskewing, and borders. No benchmark accuracy is claimed.

claims.claim: Transformers.js can run models in the browser.
claims.finding: Official docs cover browser ONNX pipelines and text/image tasks. Browser inference does not establish traffic-free operation.

claims.claim: Ollama is an open-source project with separate hosted service use.
claims.finding: Official repository identifies MIT-licensed project code. Hosted service use is not claimed to be a locally installed model or automatically free.

claims.claim: Ollama exposes local and hosted cloud API routes.
claims.finding: Official docs distinguish localhost11434 and ollama.com endpoints. The site’s selected route is checked in source below.

claims.claim: Ladybird develops an independent browser engine.
claims.finding: Official project describes an independently developed engine. No release schedule or site adoption is claimed.
Official project describes JavaScript automation without graphical rendering. Vendor speed/safety claims are not repeated.

claims.claim: Open WebUI offers self-hosted interfaces for local and cloud models.
claims.finding: Official repository supports Ollama/OpenAI-compatible providers for both routes. No deployment or unconditional license claim is made.
Official site redirects to continue.dev and states the acquisition. Checked October5,2026; no acquisition date is inferred.
